name: ChartQA
description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts with visual and logical reasoning. It covers 9,608 human-written questions (ChartQA-H) and 23,111 machine-generated questions from human-written chart summaries (ChartQA-M), totaling 20,882 charts curated from four different online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, OECD). The benchmark focuses on compositional and visual reasoning questions involving arithmetic and logical operations over real-world charts.
license: Publicly available charts used in compliance with respective source terms and conditions (Statista for academic purposes, Pew Research with attribution, OECD open data, OWID open access).
creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque (York University, Canada; Nanyang Technological University, Singapore; Salesforce Research)
citeAs: Masry, A., Long, D. X., Tan, J. Q., Joty, S., & Hoque, E. (2022). ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning.
rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista (statista.com), Pew Research (pewresearch.org), Our World In Data (ourworldindata.org), and OECD (oecd.org). For Pew, only chart images were crawled as underlying data tables were not available. For the other three sources, underlying data tables, metadata (e.g., title, chart type), SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted. Bounding box information of chart elements was extracted from SVG files to train data extraction models. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT), and additional QA pairs were generated automatically from human-written Statista chart summaries using a fine-tuned T5 model.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the Pew Research dataset, the underlying data tables are not available, so only chart images were crawled. Some machine-generated questions were invalid (incomplete or not answerable from the chart), and a heuristic filter was applied to remove questions where the answer could not be found in the chart data table. After filtering, 86.64% of manually analyzed QA pairs were complete, answerable, and correct.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Chart images and associated data from four sources: Statista (statista.com), Pew Research (pewresearch.org), Our World In Data (ourworldindata.org), and OECD (oecd.org). Human-written chart summaries from Statista were used to generate machine-based QA pairs. The dataset includes bar, line, and pie charts covering topics such as economy, politics, health, and society.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A T5 model was fine-tuned on SQuAD and applied to human-written Statista chart summaries to automatically generate QA pairs. Two T5 models were used: one for answer extraction and one for answer-aware question generation. A heuristic filter removed questions where the answer could not be found in the chart data table. The test set of the machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For human-authored QA pairs: if both annotators' answers exactly matched, the answer was considered correct; otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer. For machine-generated QA pairs: a heuristic filter removed questions where the answer could not be found in the chart data table. The test set was manually cleaned. Both ChartQA-H and ChartQA-M were randomly split into train, validation, and test sets.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA annotation was conducted via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). Workers were asked to provide two types of questions per chart: compositional questions (involving at least two mathematical/logical operations such as sum, difference, average) and visual questions (referring to visual attributes such as color, height, length of graphical marks). For each chart, workers provided two questions with answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator. If both workers' answers exactly matched, the answer was considered correct; otherwise, answers were manually checked. Workers were required to have an acceptance rate of 95% and at least 5,000 completed HITs, and were further filtered via a pretest.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. Manual checking of 500 random samples found agreement to be 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations (e.g., '3$' vs '3 dollars', '86.33' vs '86.3'). For machine-generated questions, 86.64% of 1,250 manually analyzed QA pairs were found to be complete, answerable, and correct given the chart.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 questions per chart (each answered by two annotators); workers also verified two previously asked questions by other workers per HIT.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers based in the United States (minimum wage consideration of $7.25 USD per hour used for compensation). Workers required to have an acceptance rate of 95% and at least 5,000 completed HITs. Further filtered via a pretest. All annotations were anonymized to protect privacy.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD for answer extraction and answer-aware question generation from human-written chart summaries; ChartOCR (Luo et al., 2021) extended for automatic chart data extraction; CRAFT model (Baek et al., 2019) for text recognition in chart elements.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/vis-nlp/ChartQA. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive human attributes are collected as part of this dataset. Annotator annotations were anonymized to protect privacy.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark can help develop ChartQA systems that assist users in analyzing data visualizations, potentially improving accessibility of data-driven insights. However, the models can be abused to mislead the public about chart content and implications. The authors note that model outputs cannot be guaranteed to be correct at all times.
rai:dataBiases: Politics is a common topic among all sources, particularly in the Pew dataset where nearly half of charts are about U.S. Politics & Policy (45.4%). Bar charts are the most common chart type across all datasets. The dataset is constructed from four specific online sources, which may not represent all possible chart styles or topics. Machine-generated questions may have domain mismatch issues due to T5 being fine-tuned on SQuAD.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset only covers three chart types: bar, line, and pie charts. Performance of models decreases when gold data tables are not provided, highlighting challenges in automatic data extraction from real-world charts. Current models cannot effectively handle nested arithmetic operations. The evaluation metric for chart data extraction does not take extracted textual tokens into consideration. Machine-generated questions may include invalid or unanswerable questions despite filtering. The dataset may not generalize to all real-world chart styles.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) models. The benchmark is intended to evaluate visual and logical reasoning over real-world charts. It can also be used for pretraining models before fine-tuning on other chart QA tasks. The dataset is split into train, validation, and test sets for both ChartQA-H and ChartQA-M subsets.
